presented_as: A magnetic multilayer can be thin enough for all-optical switching (three bilayers or fewer) or thick enough for long-term data retention. Not both.
source: Khalid et al., Nat Commun 17, 10843 (2026), introduction; the binary as presented by the AOS literature 2007-2026 (Stanciu 2007 through Mangin 2014, Chatterjee 2022)

O1.answer: four families of alternatives on the record, all inside the material frame
O1.record: rare-earth ferrimagnets (GdFeCo, TbFeCo); exchange-coupled ferromagnet/ferrimagnet stacks; compositional tuning; domain-size matching. The alternative that worked - redesign the light - was not among them

O2.answer: roughly two decades of field effort, no stated budget per alternative
O2.record: AOS literature 2007-2026; the thickness ceiling was treated as a material property for that entire span

O3.answer: the magnetic-materials community; the optics community was not in the loop
O3.record: UCSD Today: the two fields 'do not typically overlap'; the paper needed an optics group and a magnetics group to find the answer

O4.record: the failed and partial attempts are all citable (Stanciu 2007; Mangin 2014; Chatterjee 2022; Medapalli 2017)

O5.answer: the search was widened once, in 2026, by this study
O5.record: the widening moved the control point from the material to the optics; press quote: 'Instead of designing a new material to enable optical switching, we redesigned the light itself'

O6.answer: the constraint did not hold under direct push - it broke
O6.record: the 'three-layer ceiling' was never tested against beam geometry until this study; confined spots (below ~1.36 um at N=3) restored switching through N=9. It was a presented constraint, not a pushed one

S1.answer: researchers selecting thin stacks; the sacrificed set is the retention capacity of the storage medium and the future users of it, not the selectors
S1.record: Ndao: thickness constraint 'put a constraint on the overall thickness of the magnetic material and thus, its ability to retain memory in the long term'

S2.answer: functional position, but carried by a proxy
S2.record: weld present: 'thick vs thin' carries retention as a layer count, but the load-bearing quantity is the energy barrier per bit - never measured inside the frame

S3.record: the no-sacrifice case (thick AND optically switchable) is this study's result, but it was not specified in advance as a comparison

S4.record: no post-audit with a date and owner; the paper names future work without a schedule

S5.record: no pre-registered failure criterion. The paper's own control shows why this matters: the same fluence through a Gaussian beam permanently damages the films - a failed attempt reads as 'physics forbids it' and as 'wrong beam' identically
